bib.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
bib.venue: AAAI-24 (Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)

question: Can an LLM agent learn from its own experience across tasks, without parameter updates, and improve on unseen tasks?
hypothesis: Natural-language insights extracted from past experiences plus retrieved successful trajectories improve a ReAct agent; insights from a source task transfer to a target task.
contributions: ExpeL, an LLM agent that learns from experience without gradient updates
Evaluation on diverse tasks showing improvement on top of existing planning methods
A transfer-learning setting showing forward transfer from source to target tasks

method.summary: Stage 1 gathers trajectories on training tasks with ReAct plus Reflexion retries. Stage 2 has gpt-4-0613 distil a list of insights from fail/success pairs and chunks of L successes via ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE. At test time the task prompt gets all insights plus top-k similar successful trajectories as few-shot, single attempt.
method.task: text-based agent tasks (HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop, FEVER)

other.use: insight extraction (default) and insight transfer adaptation

inference.samples: single attempt per evaluation task; four-fold validation, mean and standard error over folds
inference.prompting: ReAct prompt with fixed few-shot examples replaced by top-k retrieved successes, plus concatenated insight list in task specification
inference.retrieval: Faiss vectorstore, kNN, all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings, maximum inner-product task similarity, top-k successful trajectories

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: exact match for HotpotQA and FEVER; completing the task in time for ALFWorld; purchasing the item matching all attributes for WebShop

eval.protocol: four-fold validation, mean and standard error over folds

results.setup: ALFWorld, gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 actor, gpt-4-0613 insights, four-fold validation, mean +- s.e.
results.table: Table 3 lower, row ExpeL (ours) 59.0 ± 0.3; row ReAct 40.0 ± 0.3
results.note: Fig 5 values not in text; prose says ExpeL 59% vs Reflexion 54% at R3, while Table 2 gives ReAct+Reflexion R3 54.4%

results.table: Table 3 upper, row ExpeL (ours) 39.0 ± 1.7; row ReAct 28.0 ± 1.4

results.claim: Insights transferred from HotpotQA to FEVER lift success rate over ReAct

results.table: Table 1, row ExpeL Transfer, 70 ± 0.7; ReAct 63 ± 0.4; Act 58 ± 0.0; w/o Task Demos 65 ± 1.7

results.claim: Combining ExpeL with Reflexion retries on ALFWorld reaches 64.2% at round 3
results.setup: ALFWorld, R1-R3 resumed from failed R0 checkpoints
results.table: Table 2, row ExpeL+Reflexion, column R3 64.2%; R0 59.0%; ReAct+Reflexion R0 40.3% R3 54.4%; retrieve-only R0 54.5% R3 60.4%

results.claim: Single-pass ExpeL matches or exceeds Reflexion at R3 without retries (as printed)

results.note: Text order is ambiguous: 40% is Reflexion R3 and 39% ExpeL on HotpotQA

results.claim: Retrieval ranking by task similarity beats reasoning similarity and random sampling on ALFWorld
results.setup: random sampled successful trajectories; reasoning similarity 48.5 ± 2.1

results.claim: LLM-generated insights beat hand-crafted; adding reflections hurts; gpt-3.5 insight extractor is worse than gpt-4
results.setup: Hand-crafted 32.0 ± 1.1; insights with reflections 29.0 ± 0.4; gpt-3.5-turbo insights 32.0 ± 0.4

limits: Text observations only; images not handled
Only closed-source API LLMs (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4) tested
All insights fit in context; lifelong use would need retrieval over insights
Prompting lacks theoretical underpinnings unlike RL
Z, H, L, k, training set sizes and number of tasks are not stated in the text; no appendix in this PDF; Fig 5 values only in figure
Behavioral analysis (Sec 5.3) is manual inspection of trajectories, anecdotal
Transfer tested on one pair only (HotpotQA to FEVER)

terms.definition: retrieve successful trajectories from the experience pool by task similarity as few-shot examples

lineage.work: Liu et al. 2022 What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3?
